summary: Node positions are lattice cells written into the markup, not the output of a simulation. Pixel position is a pure function of the cell, the system's pitch and the node's own persisted drag offset. Insertion never displaces an existing node, because a new node takes a free cell rather than a place in a flow. Density is bounded by one parameterised rule applied to every node-to-collection relationship on the board.

placement_rule.statement: px = origin + cell x pitch + persisted_offset
placement_rule.parameters_from: constitution.json -> parameters.lattice (pitch_x 300, pitch_y 180, origin_x 200, origin_y 80, cols 12, rows 11). A theme may amend the pitch under the amendment policy; it may not replace the formula.
placement_rule.cell: Declared per node in the markup as data-cell="col,row". It is authored data, part of the record, read exactly once at load by RZ.place().
placement_rule.column_semantics: Columns encode distance along the path actually travelled, left to right: col 0 is the collection the path started from, col 2 the species tier, col 4 the focus's own relations, col 6 their members, col 8 the tier beyond. Reading left is reading your own history; reading right is reading where you can go. The node you came FROM has a reserved column, so 'back' is a place rather than a guess.
placement_rule.row_semantics: Rows separate siblings of one kind within a column. They carry no ranking beyond the drawn/aggregate distinction below.
placement_rule.no_simulation: There is no force layout, no physics tick, no randomised seeding and no dependence on DOM order anywhere in assets/system.js. The only pseudo-random generator in the system is the particle field's, seeded with parameters.particles.seed, so even the decoration does not reshuffle between loads.
placement_rule.persistence: A node dragged in Arrange mode acquires a persisted offset (dx, dy) held against its record, never a new cell. The cell stays the node's identity; the offset is the user's preference. Every consumer of position -- the veins, the world-view extent, Fit, keyboard direction-finding -- reads cell + offset from RZ.nodes, so none of them can disagree. In production the offset is written to the user's own profile; a mock keeps it on the record for the life of the page.
placement_rule.user_arrangement: Arrange mode exists only to set those offsets. It changes no data and performs no traversal, and on exit it restores the camera the user had (C15, C16).

density_strategy.name: two-and-an-aggregate
density_strategy.statement: For ANY node connected to a collection of sibling nodes of one kind: if the collection has fewer than THRESHOLD members, draw every member as its own node; if it has THRESHOLD or more, draw the SHOWN highest-ranked members as nodes plus exactly ONE aggregate node standing for all the rest, labelled '+N more', which opens the full list.
density_strategy.stated_once: This rule lives in the system, on components/aggregate.html and foundations/spacing.html only. No other page restates it; a page that needs it cites it. Species is an example of the rule, never a special case.

ranking.source: the user's own garden data -- never alphabetical, never insertion order
keys_in_order: most overdue actions (days past due, descending)
needing treatment (an active problem or treatment course)
most accessed (the user's own open count, descending)
ranking.tie_break: stable by record id, so a tie does not reshuffle between loads

worked_examples.branch: not a collection of siblings of one kind -- one node per kind, so all are drawn

density_strategy.both_branches_must_be_shown: Any page or specimen demonstrating this rule shows BOTH branches side by side -- an under-threshold collection drawn in full and an at-threshold collection drawn as two-and-an-aggregate. One branch alone reads as an example rather than a rule.
density_strategy.no_silent_truncation: An aggregate is a node, not a cut. It is traversable, states its own count, and its full list is one hop away. Every list endpoint in PlantPal is paged, so '+N more opens the full list' is implementable and a kept count the interface cannot reach is a defect, not an opinion.
density_strategy.why_two: Two drawn members is the smallest number that still shows a collection is plural and lets the user compare its top-ranked items side by side; a third adds screen cost without adding that. Four is the smallest threshold at which an aggregate saves more than it costs.

growth_ceiling.drawn_nodes_bound: For a focus of degree d whose neighbours are collections, the board draws at most d x (shown + 1) member nodes at rank 'near' and their own children at rank 'far'. With shown = 2 and threshold = 4 any collection contributes at most 3 nodes whether it holds 4 members or 40,000.
growth_ceiling.practical_ceiling: About 30 nodes on screen at once -- the point at which the fringe rank stops being legible at zoom.min (0.28). The lattice is cols x rows = 12 x 11 = 132 cells, the hard ceiling on simultaneously placed nodes; beyond that the world extends by adding columns and the camera -- not the layout -- is what changes.
growth_ceiling.growth_direction: The lattice grows rightward and downward from a fixed origin. Existing cells never renumber, so a node's position is stable for the life of the record.

insertion_rule.statement: A new node takes the lowest free cell in the column its relationship to the focus assigns it, scanning rows top to bottom. Existing nodes are never renumbered, re-flowed or displaced (C8).
insertion_rule.free_cell_search_order: column fixed by relationship; rows ascending from 0; first cell not occupied by a live record wins; if the column is full the search moves to the next column of the same tier and the fact is recorded on the node.
insertion_rule.worked_case: Adding a 13th plant to My garden does not move Office Fig. Either the new plant outranks a drawn member -- in which case the loser moves into the aggregate, whose cell does not change and whose label goes from '+10 more' to '+11 more' -- or it does not, and only the aggregate's label changes. In both cases every drawn card keeps its cell.
insertion_rule.non_structural_changes: A status change, a count change, a new attachment or a health score arriving moves nothing at all (C9). Only two things change position: a user drag, and a genuinely new node taking a free cell.
insertion_rule.day_zero: An empty garden draws its first node at the cell it will keep forever, on a lattice with visible room around it. The world reads as a place with space in it rather than a failure to have data (C26).

slow_and_partial_interaction.geography_first: Cells come from the record list, which is small and arrives first. Every node is placed before any of its contents resolve, so a slow load fills cards in place and repositions nothing (C22).
slow_and_partial_interaction.unloaded_regions: An unfetched region is a node with a cell of its own, drawn as explicitly unknown. Fetching it fills that node and adds new nodes into free cells; nothing already drawn moves (C23).

verification.how_to_check_determinism: Load the page twice and diff the computed left/top of every .rz-n element. They are equal. Then reload with the DOM order of the node elements reversed: positions are unchanged, because position is read from data-cell and not from document order.
verification.how_to_check_insertion: Append a node with a free data-cell and reload. Every pre-existing node's computed left/top is unchanged.
verification.how_to_check_density: For every collection node on the board, assert drawn_members === (members < 4 ? members : 2) and that an aggregate node exists exactly when members >= 4, with its label count equal to members - 2.
verification.how_to_check_parameters: Call RZ.verifyParameters(): it compares RZ.PARAMS against the --rz-param-* custom properties computed from assets/tokens.css and returns an empty mismatch list.
